Instead of a professional medical review, I was subjected to a hostile, interrogation-style encounter.

Ms. Haden ruled out my ADHD concerns based on dangerously obsolete stereotypes, claiming that because I maintained 'eye contact' and 'sat still', I could not have the condition. This displays a complete lack of understanding of NICE Guideline NG87 and the well-documented phenomenon of 'masking' in adults. To use visual assumptions to deny a specialist referral for a neurodevelopmental condition is a gross failure of clinical duty.

Furthermore, she acted as an illegal 'gatekeeper' by pre-emptively refusing to honour my legal 'Right to Choose' (RTC). A clinician has no authority to unilaterally block a patient’s statutory rights under the NHS Constitution based on personal bias against external providers.

Her attitude towards a non-native English speaker was equally disgraceful—showing visible impatience and annoyance when asked for clarification on medical terms.

This practice is failing its patients by allowing such arrogance and clinical ignorance to persist. A formal complaint has been escalated to the Practice Manager, the ICB, and the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC).
